26.0.s.en: (3) The woman who poured the ointment

26.0.0.en: Christ came to Bethany (ch. 21:17) for the last time in His life on earth, and entered the house of a man called Simon, who was known as "the leper"; perhaps Christ had healed him of his leprosy, so he was eager to ask Him to visit him in his house.

26.0.1.en: And a woman came who loved Christ and wanted to express her love for Him, so she bought a bottle of costly perfume and poured it on His head. This woman is Mary the sister of Lazarus, as John the Evangelist mentioned (Jn 12:3), because she was known for her love of Christ, and lived in the same village, and was eager to hear His word. Matthew and Mark the Evangelists did not mention her name out of fear for her from the persecution of the Jews, whereas John wrote his Gospel a long time after the destruction of Jerusalem, when there was no longer any fear of them.

26.0.2.en: This woman wanted to express her love for Christ, for she represents the Church thankful to her Christ for His gifts and miracles and His care for her. And she declares the existence of a few believers whose hearts were filled with love in the midst of many wicked people who would cry out a few days later for His crucifixion.

26.0.3.en: "An alabaster box of very precious ointment": a small precious vessel in which costly perfumes are put, with a long neck whose mouth is sealed with a firm material, so it cannot be opened except by breaking this neck.

26.0.4.en: "On his head": the custom was to pour perfume on the head to honor beloved persons and those of high standing, and Mark also mentioned that (Mk 14:3). (As for John, he mentioned that she poured it on His feet as a sign of her humility) (and it is understood implicitly that she poured part of it on His head as was the custom).

26.0.5.en: "As he sat at meat": the custom at banquets was to sit on a couch and not a chair, leaning on the left arm on the table, while the legs stretched out on the couch and the feet pointed backward, and one ate with the right hand while leaning with his head on his left hand, and this enabled Mary to reach His head easily.

26.0.6.en: Mark, like Matthew, mentioned this event without concern for the chronological order of events, whereas John mentioned it at its time, which is six days before the Passover (Jn 12:1), that is, before Christ entered the week of His passion for the salvation of mankind, whose love for Him appeared in the person of Mary, before He endured the sufferings from the multitudes in Jerusalem. As for Matthew and Mark, they mentioned the event two days before the Passover, when Judas Iscariot took counsel to betray Christ to the Jews, to declare that if the disciple had betrayed, there are among men those who love Christ like Mary. And this event is different from the event of the sinful woman's pouring out ointment during Christ's preaching in Galilee, which took place in the house of a Pharisee also called Simon, and St. Luke mentioned it (Lk 7:37-38). Seize today as an opportunity to offer your love to Christ in prayers and hymns, for this may be the last opportunity in your life.

26.1.0.en: The disciples and all who were gathered in Simon's house saw this great love offered to Christ, and instead of feeling their shortcoming in offering love to Him like Mary, they began to blame her. The truth is that the one who declared this blame was Judas Iscariot and not the disciples, because he had the bag and was a thief (Jn 12:4-6), and by his words he stirred up the rest of the disciples and likewise those gathered in the house, so they considered her love unwise, even a waste, since in their view it would have been better for this ointment to be sold for much, and (the price) given to the poor, rather than poured on Christ.

26.1.1.en: And thus they cover their shortcoming in offering love with arguments that seem logical, namely concern for the poor, though the purpose was evil, because Judas wanted the money to be put into the bag so that he could steal a large part of it. "Much": Mark (Mk 14:5) and John (Jn 12:5) mention the price, which is estimated at three hundred denarii, a very large sum.

26.1.2.en: Do not blame those who spend a long time in prayer, or visiting holy places, or in spiritual retreats, but on the contrary, imitate them, for it is a message to you to offer love like theirs to God.

26.2.0.en: Mary was silent, but Christ defended her, affirming the greatness of her love, and He did not reject offering love to the poor as He had taught them in the previous chapter, but the poor are always present, while He, His days on earth were about to end.

26.2.1.en: And we notice the tenderness of Christ's feelings, that although He knew the evil of Judas, and that the motive for his words was love of money and not love of the poor, He did not blame him or rebuke those present, but praised Mary, and confirmed them in offering love to the poor throughout their lives. And He left an opportunity for Judas to repent and be ashamed of his hidden evil, but he, sadly, did not care, and was determined to betray Christ and sell Him to the Jews.

26.3.0.en: Then He added a second praise for the woman, which is that this love of hers is ointment poured on His body that would die on the Cross, so it is like perfumes for the burial of the body, affirming the importance of offering love. The custom among the Jews was to put ointments on the bodies of the departed, to honor them, and this custom still exists among many peoples.

26.4.0.en: Christ adds that this great love will be written in the Gospel which will be preached in the whole world, as teaching for all His children of the importance of offering pure love to Him as thanks and response to His love; and this shows the divinity of Christ, who knew that the Gospel would spread in the whole world, and that this event would be written in it. Trust that your love which you offer to Christ will be declared before all mankind on the Day of Judgment, and will remain declared forever. Let this be an encouragement to offer continual worship to God, and to do mercy with every needy person, whatever effort and money it costs you.

26.5.0.en: "The first day of the feast of unleavened bread": "first" according to the Greek translation is "proto", that is, before, and it is the same word mentioned in (Jn 1:15), when John the Baptist spoke of Christ that He was before him. The meaning of this is that Christ kept the Passover a day before the Jewish Passover, which is called "the feast of the Passover" or "the feast of unleavened bread", because unleavened bread is eaten with the Passover according to the Law (Ex 12:8, 11). And at the same time that the Jews were offering their Passover, Christ was being crucified, because He is the true Passover, signified by the slaughtered lamb that the Jews offer.

26.5.1.en: The feast of the Passover drew near, and every Jew kept the Passover inside his house with his family. But it is clear from the disciples' question to Christ about the place He chose to keep the Passover in that He had no house of His own. And Christ presented a new concept of the family, not only those bound bodily, but those bound spiritually. So the twelve gathered, and with them Christ, the head of the family, or the head of the body which is the Church. He sent them to a certain person, who tradition says was Mark the Apostle, where He kept the Passover in his house, and the household prepared the Passover with the disciples according to the Jewish Law, and it is a type of the crucified Christ who would offer Himself for the whole world the next day, that is, Great Friday.

26.5.2.en: "My time is at hand": that is, the time of His passion and crucifixion, which would be accomplished after a day, has drawn near.

26.5.3.en: "Made ready the passover": the slaughtered lamb and the bitter herbs, and the dishes and cups of wine... and so on, of what the Passover requires according to the Law.

26.6.0.en: "Even": from the third hour to the fifth hour in the evening, which is the time for eating the Passover according to the Law (Ex 12:6).

26.6.1.en: While Christ was eating the Passover with His disciples, among them Judas Iscariot the traitor who would betray Him to the Jews, Jesus bore a father's heart toward him, concerned for his salvation, and gently said to His disciples that one of them would betray Him to the Jews, and did not mention his name, in case his heart would be pricked and he would repent.

26.6.2.en: And on Thursday a group of events took place, namely:

26.6.4.en: (2) A dispute among the disciples about which of them was the greatest (Lk 22:24).

26.6.6.en: (4) Washing the disciples' feet during the eating of the Passover.

26.6.7.en: (5) Christ's announcement that one of His disciples would betray Him.

26.6.8.en: (6) The Lord's Supper and the institution of the sacrament of the Eucharist.

26.6.9.en: (7) Christ tells His disciples that they will leave Him and that Peter will deny Him.

26.6.10.en: (8) Christ's farewell discourse and His prayer, mentioned in (Jn 14-17).

26.6.11.en: (9) The singing of the hymn and the departure from the city.

26.6.14.en: God sends you many warnings and messages gently, that perhaps you may repent. So do not neglect His tender love, lest you lose your life far from Him like Judas.

26.7.0.en: The disciples were moved by the news that one of them would betray Him, and so that Christ would not leave them doubting themselves, He gave a sign of the one who would betray Him, and also to warn Judas a second time that perhaps he would repent. The sign was that the traitor would put his hand into the dish in which Christ was eating and eat from it. But sadly Judas did not take heed and ate from the dish. And from the grief of the disciples, they did not notice this sign, so they did not speak to Judas.

26.7.1.en: And it was the custom of the Jews that the master of the banquet gives the morsel to the important person sitting at the table, so the sign was an honor and love toward Judas from Christ, that perhaps it would shame him and prick his heart so that he would repent of his evil, for Judas put his hand into Christ's dish, and Christ put out His hand and gave him the morsel.

26.7.2.en: And it is clear that the morsel was from the Passover meal, and after it Judas went out and did not eat of the Lord's Supper.

26.8.0.en: Christ warned Judas for the third time, declaring woe to this traitor, for his eternal torment would be severe, indeed it would have been good for him if he had not been born, so as not to commit this great betrayal. And Christ made clear that He must be delivered to the Jews and die by His own will through one of His beloved ones who betrays Him (Ps 41:9), so that His disciples may be reassured that He does this for their salvation and the salvation of all mankind, but here He only warns Judas and gives him an opportunity to repent and review himself.

26.9.0.en: Judas dared (not out of repentance but out of hypocrisy) and asked Christ: "Master, is it I?" (the one who betrays You). Christ answered him, as a fourth warning to him: "Thou hast said." This is a Jewish expression meaning agreement. And Judas did not take heed, because love of money had blinded his eyes, and the disciples likewise did not take heed and understand, because of their astonishment that one of them would be His betrayer, and their immersion in grief over what would happen to their Teacher. Hasten today to repentance and confession while you have the opportunity, before a day comes on which you lose your sense of repentance, however many divine warnings you are given.

26.10.0.en: After Christ finished eating the Passover with His disciples, He instituted the sacrament of thanksgiving, that is, He gave them His most holy Body and Blood, for He took bread and blessed it and changed it into His Body, and gave it to them to eat, declaring that this is His true Body. And likewise the cup, He changed the wine in it into His Blood, declaring that it would be shed for all mankind on the Cross.

26.10.1.en: And thus He gave His Church the greatest of the sacraments, the sacrament of Communion, that we may be united with Him throughout the ages, so that we do not only see Christ as the people of His time saw Him, but touch Him and He enters into us, and unites with us, so that He lives in us and we in Him, and we also are united with one another by each of us partaking of His Body and Blood, so we all become members of His body which is the Church.

26.10.2.en: "And as they were eating": that is, immediately after they finished eating the Passover, He instituted the sacrament of the Eucharist (thanksgiving), because the Passover is a type of it.

26.10.3.en: "Bread": it is leavened bread, because we are a day before the Passover. Therefore the Church offers on the altar leavened bread and not unleavened, because Christ bore our sins, which the leaven indicates, and died on the Cross, and so wiped away every punishment from us.

26.10.4.en: "The disciples": they represent the whole Church of the New Testament, and therefore in the rite of the Liturgy, the priest divides the Body of Christ into 12 parts representing the twelve disciples around the middle part called the Lordly part, that is, the Spadikon, that is, Christ in the midst of His people, or Christ the head of the Church.

26.10.5.en: "My blood": which the blood of animals in the Old Testament signifies, and without shedding of blood is no remission (Heb 9:22).

26.10.6.en: "The new testament": blood was used anciently to confirm covenants by the shedding of the blood of animals, as happened with Abraham (Gen 15:9-19).

26.10.7.en: "Many": a declaration that Christ's redemption is for the whole world, and everyone who believes in Him and partakes of this Blood receives salvation from his sins.

26.10.8.en: "For the remission of sins": an affirmation that the sacrament of thanksgiving forgives sins, sharing in this with the sacrament of repentance and confession.

26.11.0.en: Christ declares a new truth to His disciples and to all who believe in Him, which is that He will not perform the sacrament of thanksgiving again on earth, that is, He will not change the fruit of the vine, which is the wine, into His Blood, until He drinks it with His children in the eternal Kingdom, but in a new form suited to their existence in the Spirit, that is, our love and union and growth in the knowledge of Christ extend into the eternal Kingdom, not by partaking of bread and wine that change into His Body and Blood, but we are united with Him in a spiritual way suited to our spiritual state in heaven.

26.11.1.en: "That day": a day of gathering with you in the eternal Kingdom.

26.12.0.en: "Sung an hymn": the Jews were accustomed to sing Psalms 115 and 116 at the end of their eating of the Passover. And after their singing, Christ spoke to them a long talk, and then prayed His intercessory prayer (Jn 14-17). They offered prayers and hymns fitting for the sacrament of thanksgiving, as happens in the Divine Liturgy during the distribution of the Holy Mysteries, and He went out with them to the Mount of Olives near Jerusalem, where He used to spend periods of quiet retreat with them, to bid them His last farewell before He died.

26.12.1.en: Christ was not content with sermons and counsels for you, but gives you the power to carry them out, which is His Body and Blood that you partake of and that unite with you, and so work in you to carry out His word, and the hardest commandments become easy by His power. So take care to partake regularly of the Holy Mysteries, because they are the greatest power in the world that keeps you from the wars of the devil and makes you grow in the knowledge of God every day.

26.13.0.en: As Christ was walking with His disciples to the Mount of Olives, He told them a bitter truth, which is their doubting Him that He is the Christ the Savior, since they were still thinking of Him as an earthly king, so when they see Him arrested, they doubt Him. And this is a fulfilment of the prophecies of the Old Testament, that Satan will smite the Shepherd by arresting Him and crucifying Him, and His flock will be scattered (Zech 13:7).

26.13.1.en: But when Satan smote Christ by His crucifixion, Christ turned this blow upon Satan, so He bound him with His Cross, and gathered all His children to save and redeem them.

26.13.3.en: "The flock": they are the disciples of Christ.

26.14.0.en: Despite the bitter truth, which is the doubt of Christ's disciples nearest to Him concerning Him, He will accomplish their salvation on the Cross, and die, and rise from the dead, and appear to them in Galilee where He was accustomed to walk with them in the fields from city to city. So He encourages them again that He will rise, but sadly they did not take in His words; and Christ repeated that He would appear to them in Galilee at His appearing after His resurrection to the Magdalene (ch. 28:10, 7).

26.14.1.en: The tender God loves you despite the weakness of your faith, and encourages you by His word and His gifts. So stand firm during the affliction, confident that He will support you and appear clearly in your life.

26.15.0.en: Peter rushed forward with human emotion, declaring his faith in Christ and his steadfastness in Him whatever the circumstances, even if everyone doubted Him. So Christ made clear to him that, because of his weakness, he would not endure facing the difficult situation, which is His being arrested to be killed. And then, that is, on this night, before the cock crows, he would deny Him, not only once, but three times, as confirmation of his human weakness.

26.15.1.en: Peter's words show his love for Christ, but at the same time show his mistake in rashness and pride, in feeling that he was better than others in the steadfastness of his faith.

26.16.0.en: Peter affirmed his clinging to Christ even unto death, and likewise all the disciples. And Christ did not answer them, so that they might see for themselves the extent of their weakness, for in the hour of affliction, at His arrest, all forsook Him and fled (v. 56).

26.16.1.en: Ask for the help of the Holy Spirit, and He will support you at the time of affliction so that you hold fast to your faith, for it is hard for you to face affliction alone.

26.17.0.en: "A place": a field or a place with crops, and it seems that its owner knew Christ, so He was accustomed to go there with His disciples.

26.17.1.en: "Here": probably at the entrance of the garden.

26.17.2.en: "The disciples": He means the eight disciples, because Judas had left them. And the three, Peter, James and John, would enter with Him into the garden.

26.17.3.en: "Even unto death": intense sorrow can lead to death, so He expresses the severity of the sorrows He feels.

26.17.4.en: Christ arrived with His disciples at the Mount of Olives in a garden where it seems He was accustomed to retreat with them, and it is called the garden of Gethsemane, which means "oil press", and it is near Jerusalem, and He left His disciples to retire or pray, and the three nearest to Him advanced with Him, Peter and James and John the sons of Zebedee, to pray apart, for these three had spiritual stature, so He could reveal to them what was in His soul, and He said to them: "My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death".

26.17.5.en: And this sorrow was because He, the Righteous One, would bear the sins of the whole world, for how can righteousness agree with sin?! How painful that is to soul and spirit, in addition to His grief for the Jews who would reject Him and crucify Him while He seeks their salvation.

26.17.6.en: And He asked His three disciples to pray, indeed to continue in prayer with watchfulness and vigilance.

26.17.7.en: The disciples were moved, though they did not understand exactly all the dimensions of this sorrow, because the Holy Spirit had not yet descended upon them for them to understand the salvation offered to them.

26.17.8.en: This confirms the humanity of Christ, for He needed psychologically His close friends, the disciples, to pray with Him in the garden, and the three disciples especially to be nearer to Him in the depth of the garden.

26.18.0.en: After that, He left the three disciples and advanced alone to pray, and He withdrew from His disciples so as not to disturb them if they saw the intensity of His sorrow. And He felt the difficulty of the cup of suffering, not only the bodily in the crucifixion and death, but rather the psychological when everyone would leave Him, and even more the spiritual by bearing the sins of the world while He is the Righteous and Holy One. And this is a confirmation of His humanity that suffers bodily and psychologically, and in order to show the extent of His obedience and submission to the will of the divinity in Him, so He speaks with the Father, saying: "not my will, but thine, be done".

26.18.1.en: "Fell on his face": and here, He teaches us the rite of prayer and prostrations (metanoias), that is, bowing down and humbling ourselves before God in afflictions, that He may support us by His grace.

26.18.2.en: "O my Father": a declaration of the importance of feeling God's fatherhood in prayer, so that it may support us in our afflictions. "The cup": the sufferings He would meet.

26.18.3.en: It is your right to cry out to God in all your afflictions, and ask for what you need, but quickly follow it with the prayer "thy will be done", and you surrender your life to Him, and leave Him, the tender Father, to choose for you what suits you, and support you in your afflictions.

26.19.0.en: "The disciples": that is, the three, Peter, James and John.

26.19.1.en: "One hour": a short period, and not precisely a clock hour.

26.19.2.en: After He prayed alone, He returned to His three disciples, and found them asleep from weariness and sorrow, so He woke them to pray after gently rebuking them for their sleeping, directing His words to Peter: "What, could ye not watch with me one hour?"

26.19.3.en: And He declared the importance of prayer with spiritual vigilance, so that the devil does not make us fall into temptations and sins. And He also affirmed that the spirit, if it is active and cares for prayer, can support the weak body that inclines to laziness and rest. So He gently encourages them that their spirits can be active, and so support their body that is weak from weariness and sorrow.

26.19.4.en: Complete your prayers and readings at night however exhausted you are, for God rejoices in your love however weak your concentration in them.

26.20.0.en: Christ returned to pray alone with the same words, and came back to His disciples and found them asleep a second time. And this confirms that in the hour of affliction they were not able to stand with Him; and how this increased His sorrows. But He did not weary, but went a third time to pray to the same effect.

26.20.1.en: Persevere in your prayers and your relationship with God, and hold fast to your principles however much those around you abandon you or even resist you, for Christ teaches you the importance of persistence in prayer, especially in times of affliction.

26.21.0.en: When He returned to them, He rebuked them with disapproval for the third time, not only the three but all the disciples, saying: "Sleep on now, and take your rest". So they began to take heed; then He told them that the hour of His arrest and the beginning of His entering into the sufferings of the crucifixion had come, and called them to wake up quickly, because Judas who would betray Him to the Jews had drawn near with the Temple guards to arrest Him.

26.21.1.en: It is to be noted that these Temple guards were Jews and not Romans; they were a body of guards appointed by the priests to maintain the order of the Temple, since the Law did not permit Roman soldiers to enter the Temple lest it be defiled.

26.22.0.en: "One of the twelve": to show his betrayal, since he was one of the close ones, so how could he betray his Master?!

26.22.1.en: "A great multitude": includes the Jewish Temple guards and the Roman soldiers assigned to guard the Temple from outside, and the soldiers of the high priest, and some of the followers of the priests who resist Christ.

26.22.2.en: "Great": a large number came to ensure the arrest of Christ, lest His disciples and those who love Him resist that. "The elders of the people": some members of the Sanhedrin.

26.22.3.en: "Kissed him": Judas used the expression of love, which is the kiss, in hypocrisy, to carry out his betrayal by the arrest of Christ. While Christ was waking His disciples, His disciple Judas Iscariot came with a great number of soldiers armed with swords and staves, and gave greeting to Christ and kissed Him, and this was the agreed sign, that is, to arrest the one he kisses, and that was for certainty, for Christ was known to the multitudes, but so that the men of the chief priests and the elders of the people would not err and arrest another who resembled Him.

26.23.0.en: Christ rebuked Judas and warned him, for perhaps he would repent, asking him: "Friend, wherefore art thou come?" Perhaps he would be ashamed of what he was doing (which is betraying Christ and delivering Him to the Jews), but sadly he continued in his evil, and commanded the crowd with him, and they arrested Christ.

26.23.1.en: Do not make light of the successive opportunities for repentance that God allows you, so that you do not have the fate of Judas in the end.

26.24.0.en: "One": he is Peter (Jn 18:10-11), and Matthew did not mention him out of fear for him from the persecution of the Jews, whereas John mentioned him because he wrote his Gospel after the destruction of Jerusalem, and there was no longer any fear after the breaking of the power of the Jews.

26.24.1.en: "Smote off his ear": Peter was a fisherman and had no experience in using the sword, so he could only strike the ear of this servant and cut it off.

26.24.2.en: "His place": that is, its sheath (its scabbard).

26.24.3.en: Peter was disturbed when he saw his Teacher and beloved arrested, so he rushed and took a sword, because the disciples had two swords as mentioned in (Lk 22:38). And in an attempt to defend Christ, he cut off the ear of the high priest's servant, named Malchus (Jn 18:10), but Christ commanded him to return his sword to its sheath, and declared that whoever lives by violence will suffer from violence.

26.24.4.en: And Christ wanted to remove evil from the heart of Peter and all His disciples toward those who are hostile to them, for He came to establish love in the hearts of His children even toward enemies, and to affirm that love is stronger than violence. And by His death that was about to be accomplished, He was able to trample death, and save His children from their sins, and bind the devil, and then rise victorious, declaring the victory and power of love.

26.25.0.en: "Thinkest thou": meaning: do you doubt my power after you have seen my many miracles?

26.25.1.en: "Twelve legions of angels": that is, instead of the twelve weak disciples.

26.25.2.en: Christ warned Peter and all the disciples of His great power, for the hosts of heaven are all under His obedience, that is, the angels, each of whom has power greater than all mankind, and He can ask for more than twelve legions of them, and He means a very abundant number. But by His will He surrenders Himself and dies to save His children, as the prophecies were written about Him in the Old Testament, such as (Isa 53:7).

26.26.0.en: Christ also rebuked the crowd for coming out by night with swords and staves to arrest Him, as though they were arresting a fugitive thief, though He had been with them every day teaching in the Temple in the midst of the multitudes, and that was to show their deceit and weakness, for they came to arrest Him away from the multitudes so that no one would resist them; and perhaps by this rebuke He wanted to give them an opportunity to repent also.

26.26.1.en: "Daily": that is, many days, in which He taught openly in the Temple.

26.26.2.en: "I sat": that is, I taught quietly, and did not make a disturbance, as criminals do.

26.26.3.en: "Teaching in the temple": that is, openly and clearly before all, so there was no need for you to come by night as though I were a fugitive from justice.

26.26.4.en: "Ye laid no hold on me": because you have no charges against me, and because of your fear of the people who regard me as a great teacher.

26.27.0.en: Christ affirmed that what they were doing was the fulfilment of the prophecies of the prophets, and when they arrested Him, all the disciples were afraid and fled, so as not to be arrested, for their refuge and strength were lost, since they had thought that He would protect them from the violence of the Romans and the Jews (Isa 63:3, 5). And of course, their leaving Christ caused Him psychological pain, because of their retreating from their promises not to leave Him even unto death. But in His love, He found an excuse for them, and forgave them their weakness after His resurrection.

26.27.1.en: Do not be alarmed if your loved ones leave you in the hour of affliction, for God will not leave you. And do not be angry with them, but find an excuse for them, which is human weakness.

26.28.0.en: Jesus was led to the palace of Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders were gathered in preparation for His trial (see the commentary on v. 66).

26.29.0.en: Despite the weakness of the disciples and their flight, Peter's love drove him to follow the crowd that arrested Christ, and to go in and sit in the outer court of the high priest's house, to know what they would do to his Teacher. John his fellow disciple also followed him, who was able to enter inside the house, since he had a relationship with the high priest (Jn 18:15), but both of them, despite their love, were not able to defend Him because of their human weakness.

26.30.0.en: Throughout Christ's life the Jews were unable to find one fault in Him, despite their many attempts to catch Him in a word. And in this trial, they were insistent on finding some fault in Him, even by false witness. So they gathered many to fabricate false charges against Him, but they did not agree, and their lying appeared before those present, so they could not rely on all the false testimonies.

26.30.1.en: Then in the end two men rose up to bear false witness against Christ, namely His saying that He could destroy the temple of Solomon and build it in three days. And this did not happen, but rather He said to His disciples: "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up" (Jn 2:19). And Christ meant the temple of His body, that is, that they would crucify Him, and He would rise on the third day. And the two could not prove their testimony, so the whole council was in perplexity, and unable to accuse Christ.

26.30.2.en: And the priests understood Christ's words as having been said about His body and not about the Temple, as is proved by their words to Pilate after the death of Christ, when they said: "Sir, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again" (ch. 27:63).

26.30.3.en: "Two false witnesses": because the number two is the minimum number for the acceptance of testimony according to the Law.

26.31.0.en: The high priest was perplexed, since he did not find any charge against Christ, so he asked Him why He did not answer the testimony that the two witnesses presented, that perhaps he might find in His answer some error to condemn Him for.

26.32.0.en: "I adjure thee": that is, the oath by God as the Law prescribes to confirm speech.

26.32.1.en: Christ was silent, and did not respond to all the false accusations, because He knows their hatred and resistance to Him, and that they did not want to know the truth.

26.32.2.en: And in perplexity and distress, the high priest asked Him whether He was the expected Messiah, that is, the Christ the Son of God? And sadly, he did not mean to understand, because the prophecies he knew in the Holy Scriptures confirm that it is He, but he wanted to catch some fault in Him, such as the claim that He is the Christ while being merely an ordinary man.

26.33.0.en: Christ answered him, saying: "Thou hast said", that is, agreement. And He answered thus to end their perplexity, and give them an opportunity and a proof to crucify Him and kill Him, for He surrenders Himself by His will for our salvation.

26.33.1.en: Rather, He declared His divinity plainly, saying that He would sit on the right hand of the divine Majesty, that is, in the fullness of divine power and glory, and remain in His glory until His second coming on the clouds of heaven to judge the world as the prophecies mentioned (Ps 110:1), and as He Himself declared in His talk about the judgment (ch. 24:30).

26.33.2.en: "Hereafter": that is, after hours, He will accomplish redemption on the Cross, and ascend to His glory in heaven. "The Son of man": that is, the One whom you see in me in the image of weakness as a man will be changed after hours into His heavenly glory, and He is the One who will judge you. If you are trying me now, I will judge you with an eternal judgment on the last day.

26.34.0.en: At last the high priest found a reason to sentence Him to death, so he rent his clothes to express his distress at this blasphemy. And this rending meant the end of the Jewish priesthood, so that the Christian priesthood would begin with Christ the High Priest who offered Himself as a sacrifice on the Cross, saving all who believe in Him.

26.34.1.en: And this shows the extent of the evil of the high priest, who did not examine whether He was the Christ the Son of God or not, but considered His words blasphemy, and took it as an opportunity to condemn Him, and stirred up the council to issue the sentence of death on Christ.

26.35.0.en: The high priest asked the council to judge Christ, so they issued their sentence of death on Him as a blasphemer, and the Law requires the stoning of the blasphemer, but they did not stone Him for fear of the people, but asked the civil authority to confirm the sentence of death, and obtained that through Pilate, who ordered His crucifixion, because the Romans sentence criminals to crucifixion.

26.35.1.en: It is worth mentioning that Christ was tried six times:

26.35.2.en: The first: in the house of Annas, the father-in-law of Caiaphas and the former high priest (Jn 18:19-24).

26.35.3.en: The second: mentioned in (v. 57), and it was in the house of Caiaphas the present high priest, where the priests and scribes and elders of the people gathered, to try Him and catch faults in Him according to their law, so that they might have a pretext for killing Him.

26.35.4.en: And He was tried the third trial on Friday morning (ch. 27:1-2), before the Sanhedrin council, because it is not valid according to the Law to issue a sentence at night, so they adopted the judgment of Caiaphas on Friday morning (Jn 18:28). Then He was tried civilly three other times, two before Pilate (ch. 27:2-24; Mk 15:

26.36.0.en: The mockery of Christ and His torture began, for the soldiers of the chief priests spat on Him and buffeted Him, and covered His face and struck Him, saying: "Prophesy unto us, thou Christ, Who is he that smote thee?" That is, He claims prophecy while He is a weak man who cannot defend Himself.

26.36.1.en: † Christ endured all the bodily and psychological torment in silence because of His love for us. So remember that your sins are what caused your Redeemer all these insults, so that you may reject them in shame and embarrassment, and so repent, and God will forgive you.

26.37.0.en: While Peter was sitting in the outer court of the high priest's house, a maid saw him and said to those sitting that he was one of Christ's disciples, and she had seen him with Him among the multitudes when He was teaching and working miracles. But Peter denied that, declaring that he knew nothing about Christ, saying: "I know not what thou sayest", in order to protect himself from their violence and arrest. And the cock crowed here for the first time (Mk 14:68), and that was around midnight, at the beginning of Christ's trial in the house of Caiaphas, which lasted about three hours, and this is the first denial.

26.38.0.en: Peter was afraid and rose from his place, and stood in the porch, that is, a passage outside the house, and another maid saw him, perhaps she had heard the words of the first maid, and said to those standing that he was one of the followers of Jesus. But Peter denied, and even began to swear that he did not know Him, and this is the second denial. And bitterness had begun inside his heart after hearing the crowing of the cock, for he was torn between his fear of the Jews and his distress with himself for denying Christ.

26.39.0.en: Then a group of men standing in the outer court came, and saw him speaking with the maid, and testified that he was one of Christ's disciples, and the proof was the speech he uttered, for it was like that of the people of Galilee, since the manner of speaking differs from one region to another.

26.39.1.en: And it is understood from the other Gospels that many recognized him and declared that he was one of the disciples of Jesus, that is, they besieged him with accusations, but he answered them with denial.

26.40.0.en: Peter began to deny and swear, affirming that he did not know Him, and even cursed, to confirm his denial, so as to save himself from their hands.

26.40.1.en: And by this, he denied Christ a third time. And here the cock crowed its second crowing, and that was in the second watch, that is, around three in the morning.

26.40.2.en: Fear makes a person lose his balance, so he easily falls into many sins... Hold fast to God and ask for His help, and you will flee from fear and all the sins that follow it.

26.41.0.en: When the cock crowed, Peter remembered Christ's warning to him that he would deny Him, so he came to himself, and went out from the high priest's palace, feeling his betrayal of Christ his beloved and Teacher, and offered repentance from the heart with many tears.

26.41.1.en: For though Christ had not yet risen from the dead and shown His power, love moved Peter, and he repented because he had denied the love of his Lord.

26.41.2.en: If you sin, love is the first mover of the life of repentance. Remember God's love for you and His care for you, and His death on the Cross for you, and His broken Body and shed Blood which you partook of from the altar, so that you return by repentance, and do not persist in your sins whatever the temptations and motives around you, for nothing in all the world is dearer than love.
